targets.location: Proof 5.1, the step that puts the disk-map interior in finite PL general position relative to S
targets.evidence: The proof assumes relative PL approximation and general position, then infers that the disk-map preimage of S is a finite union of circles. Its listed triangulation and Loop-theorem inputs do not state or prove this construction for the arbitrary disk map. Close the gap with a finite relative PL or smooth approximation and general-position theorem preserving the boundary class and collar, or prove that construction. The assigned Gordon–Luecke proof uses only this supplier’s first assertion, so the gap is in its separate incompressibility criterion. This is current-run draft content with no item carrier in a current batch manifest, so no exact producer batch is available.

The current proof says to “put [the map's] interior in finite PL general position relative to S” and then infers that the preimage is a finite union of circles. The cited triangulation input supplies compatible triangulations, and the PL Loop theorem input's Facts F1 only says continuous maps of finite polyhedral pairs admit simplicial approximations homotopic as maps of pairs. Neither states or proves the relative general-position construction for this arbitrary cap map while preserving its boundary class and collar. A standard relative PL approximation and general-position argument closes this small gap.

decisions.evidence: Independent current Proof 5.1 review confirms an omitted relative approximation/general-position justification: compatible triangulation alone does not establish that a cap can be changed relative to its boundary collar with finite circle preimage. Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology, Corollary 3.3, printed p.48, uses transversality and the same innermost-circle argument. A smooth approximation relative to a collar followed by transversality to the two-sided surface gives a compact one-dimensional preimage, hence finitely many circles; this standard local justification is nonfatal. Current first-assertion Proof 1.1–4.1 and its actual triangulation, PL Loop, subdivision, rounding and collar interfaces were independently checked for the assigned application. Gordon–Luecke Proof 2.1 supplies a continuous cap, whole torus, trivial normal subgroup and connected orientable smooth exterior; it uses no part of the separate criterion. Source remains read-only and unchanged. Owner should add the relative approximation/transversality justification or exact prerequisite to Proof 5.1; no source repair is claimed.
